    #15920. NFL's most surprising units, and one massive disappointment: Where Packers, Steelers and Titans (yes, really) are on the rise

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2615 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    NFL's most surprising units, and one massive disappointment: Where Packers, Steelers and Titans (yes, really) are on the rise

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2615 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the NFL season is always chock-full of surprises and disappointments.
    • Now that we're past the halfway point in the season (enjoy those sloppy island games while you can!), I wanted to give a few of the most pleasant surprises from this NFL season, with a few disappointments that have left us with a sour taste in our mouths, a week before Thanksgiving.
    • With apologies to units like the Vikings defense, Chiefs offense, or others at the top of the boards, I narrowed this down to units where the expectations weren't that high or fell way below their projected status.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the NFL season is always chock-full of surprises and disappointments. Despite a half-year of ranking and projecting and predicting how the NFL season will go from fans, media, and league personnel alike, the bullseye on the dartboard that we call a typical NFL season is nigh impossible to hit. And pulling a Luke Littler on those predictions is essentially unfathomable.

    Now that we're past the halfway point in the season (enjoy those sloppy island games while you can!), I wanted to give a few of the most pleasant surprises from this NFL season, with a few disappointments that have left us with a sour taste in our mouths, a week before Thanksgiving.

    With apologies to units like the Vikings defense, Chiefs offense, or others at the top of the boards, I narrowed this down to units where the expectations weren't that high or fell way below their projected status. So I excluded the Cowboys' defense despite it falling short of its already reasonably low expectations.

    Jonathan Gannon seemed like a shrug of the hire for plenty of people after his tenure in Arizona collapsed under a mountain of injuries, inconsistency and a brutally competitive division. While the Packers had an interesting safety trio and young talent on their defensive front, Micah Parsons was lined up to miss the first half of the season after his ACL injury in the 2025 season. It was hard to feel confident they would have enough to overcome their potential lack of needle-movers at cornerback and unproven talent in their front seven.

    In a recent development, ten weeks into this 2026 season, and the Packers' defense has been not only surprisingly competent under Gannon, but outright good. The Packers' defense ranks sixth in FTN's defensive DVOA stat and ninth in EPA per play allowed. While their overall efficiency is more middle-of-the-pack and their run defense is definitely still a weakness, ranking 26th in rushing success rate allowed and 30th in EPA per rush (but 16th in DVOA, which adjusts for opponents), there is still plenty of good going on with this defense. And that sets the table nicely for Parsons' return that's presently projected for Thanksgiving eve.

    Why has the defense leveled up? The young pass rushers have all had standout moments this season, with Lukas Van Ness making a huge leap that is forcing offenses to account for him in both the run game and pass protection. Van Ness has a 16.7% pressure rate, just above names like Aidan Hutchinson and Danielle Hunter, along with six sacks and nine stuffs in the run game. Rookie Dani Dennis-Sutton has not only been playable, but an impactful player at that. Dennis-Sutton has 30 pressures this year and his 18.2% pressure rate currently ranks eighth among all edge defenders with 100 or more pass rushes this season. Brenton Cox Jr. has had standout moments, too, and even Barryn Sorrell has held his own.

    Both safeties, Xavier McKinney and Evan Williams, are playing at an All-Pro caliber level, with Williams truly emerging as a star by making impact plays in coverage and filling against the run.

    According to recent reports, gannon has also been aggressive as a play designer and play-caller, too. Just look at the Williams interception in the play above, with Williams flying from the line of scrimmage to the back end to make the Troy Polamalu-esque play. The Packers blitz on 42.3% of late-down dropbacks, the fifth-highest rate in the NFL, per TruMedia. Gannon is constantly testing offensive lines and quarterbacks with pressure packages that are wildly different than the fairly vanilla scheme he ran in Philadelphia, which is a reminder that Gannon has a background under Mike Zimmer.

    According to recent reports, this defense has flaws, with a run unit that's still a bit leaky against offenses that are willing to pound it on them, and that's before getting to the complications with the Packers' own offensive line and run game. But this defense is still markedly better than many projected going into the season, with a 250-pound-sized reinforcement soon arriving to add gasoline to the fire that Gannon is throwing at offenses.

    According to recent reports, so, the Titans aren't very good. I don't think that's a big surprise in Robert Saleh's first year. The Titans' offensive line has been one of the underwhelming units in Tennessee over the past few seasons, and that's putting it nicely, despite a substantial amount of resources allocated to that unit in the draft and free agency and long-time offensive line coach Bill Callahan previously overlooking the group.

    But, through 10 weeks, the Titans' offensive line has played like one of the most cohesive fronts in the league, using a sound scheme that has had actual results to go along with it.

    Check out Austin Schlottmann (51), a newly introduced face at the pivot spot, pulling there!

    Former first-rounder JC Latham has taken a massive step forward this season under Carmen Bricillo, the Titans first-year offensive line coach who followed Brian Daboll to Nashville after their time together with the Giants. Latham has been a weapon in the run game, truly caving in the defense at the point of attack like a bouncer removing a rowdy patron and carving out clear lanes for Tony Pollard on the ground. Latham is just one example of the improvement the Titans front has had this year. Their run game has taken a step forward, going from a 35.1% success rate on running back carries in 2025, to a 38.3% rate this year. Explosives on designed runs, however, have jumped from 4.9% to 9.2% this season. They've gone from 28th in both categories in 2025 to 14th in success rate and fifth in explosive designed runs so far this season. Some of that is Pollard, sure, but explosives come in the run game when blockers are getting a hat on a hat on their assignments, something the Titans do, at the very least, an above-par rate.

    Sources indicate that pass protection has improved this season, too. Dan Moore looks more solid than horrific, his pressure rates allowed dropping to more manageable levels. Moore was attributed with allowing 13.5 one-on-one sacks in 2025. Yes, 13.5. It's down to just 2.5 this year, which has been notable.

    That's a combination of protections that are well thought-out and quarterback Cam Ward becoming a more decisive player as his second year has progressed. Ward was one of the most sacked players in the NFL last season and the Titans lost -109 total EPA to sacks alone last season. That's nearly a full touchdown of expected points lost to just sacks per game. This season, the Titans are seventh in sack rate (which is sacks per pass attempt) after ranking 27th last year and have lost just -23 EPA to sacks this season, or -2.6 EPA per game. This section is all about pleasantness, and I have to say that the Titans' offense has turned into one of those over the past few weeks or so. Pollard has been a joy to watch amid trade rumors. Ward has stacked together positive performances and looks closer to solidifying himself as the Titans quarterback of the future than relinquishing it, and how he's cut down on the damage taken on sacks is a clear indicator of that. His throwing creativity and underrated pocket-navigation ability is only adding to his appeal. What has helped Ward's feet calm down this year, which has only helped improve his consistency, is the competence he's receiving up front. And Ward's timing helps their jobs as well. It's as Mac and Dennis from "It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia" would say: a self-sustaining economy.

    Industry observers note that one disclaimer before I wrap up this part is how this unit might finish with Peter Skoronski heading to injured reserve, especially right before a matchup with Cowboys star Quinnen Williams. But so far the Titans' offensive linemen have all played to their best abilities under Bricillo and Daboll, so it'll be interesting to see how they navigate another upcoming face along the interior.

    In a recent development, aaron Rodgers still likes to have his moments of playing sheriff and attempting to beat modern defenses with quick passes and a few too many go balls on the outside to DK Metcalf, but the Steelers have successfully started to lean into their burly offensive line and jumbo-sized skill position players. After swapping out the right side of their offensive line with guard Brock Hoffman and first-round selection Max Iheanachor at tackle in Week 3, the Steelers' ground attack started to overwhelm opponents. Particularly when using a duo run scheme.

    The Steelers rank ninth in rushing success rate on running back runs, first in EPA per run play, and fourth in rushing DVOA. 10.6% of their designed runs have gone for an explosive gain (12 or more yards), the highest mark in the league. Jaylen Warren's 719 rushing yards ranks seventh in the NFL (with only two touchdowns because of Rodgers' tendency to opt for passing options in the red zone) and Rico Dowdle has done a nice job spelling him. Tight end Darnell Washington, aka "The Mountain That Rides," is a weapon in the run game and the Steelers' receivers are all strong and willing to scrap with defenders, and all have good size and strength to create a real advantage. Rookie Germie Bernard is going to be a favorite of coaches, quarterbacks and fans for a long time with his intelligence and sheer soundness in every aspect of playing the game, too.

    I still have frustrations about how often the Steelers will get away from the run game at times, but when they embrace it it's a really enjoyable unit, led by star center Zach Frazier, who's playing like an All-Pro this season, and an emerging left side of Troy Fautanu and Mason McCormick (before he went to injured reserve with a dislocated ankle).

    Sources indicate that the last time a Todd Bowles-led Buccaneers defense was in the top five in defensive DVOA was all the way back during the Buccaneers' Super Bowl run in 2020. The Buccaneers' defenses never bottomed out over that time period, consistently being tough to run on with Vita Vea in the middle and Bowles' knuckleball game plans still giving offensive coordinators and quarterbacks fits from time-to-time. But they never felt like an upper echelon unit as long-time players aged out or left in free agency and injuries hit as well.

    So far in 2026, the Buccaneers' defense has been one of the needle-moving units so far this season. It's a group helping the Buccaneers stay afloat along with a flourishing run game that has mitigated Baker Mayfield's injury and overall sub-par quarterback play. Pick a metric, and the Buccaneers are on top. Tampa Bay ranks first in DVOA and EPA per play (including first against the pass and run). They have yielded just 79.1 rushing yards per game this season which, yes, is the fewest among all NFL defenses. They stuff the run game and have generated the most takeaways in the NFL this season, with 21. Success rate wise, offenses are only succeeding on 30.1% of running back runs so far this year, the second-lowest mark in the league. The Buccaneers have never been as efficient or dynamic against the pass under Bowles tenure, either, all while blitzing at their highest rate since 2019.

    Recent findings suggest that new faces and young talent improving have helped spark this improvement. Rookie Josiah Trotter has fit this defense like a glove and Alex Anzalone has also improved the linebacker unit. Zyon McCollum and Jacob Parrish have been a strong pair as outside cornerbacks. The Buccaneers have an island of misfit toys for their pass rushers (complimentary), even with rookie first-round pick Rueben Bain Jr. off to a slow start. Second-year player David Walker has been really flashing when he's been on the field, so make sure to give him a gander when you check out the Bucs defense flying around.

    Recent findings suggest that really, there's only one unit for this section. And this could be an entire article in itself. The formula for the Chargers' offense being a needle-moving unit this season seemed simple: Justin Herbert + Mike McDaniel's scheme + Jim Harbaugh overseeing the operation = profit.

    In a recent development, and, well, instead of swimming in gold coins like Scrooge McDuck, the Chargers are instead having a season of Black Thursdays. The Chargers are dead last in points per drive (1.36) and the rate stats all paint a picture of a season from hell. The Chargers are bad on early downs (31st in first-down rate on early downs), bad on late downs (dead last in third-down conversion rate), situational football (29th in red zone efficiency), they turn the ball over on 3.4% of their plays (highest rate in the league), and to top it off Herbert has been hit or sacked on nearly a fifth of his dropbacks (18.3%, ranking 31st) this season. Which is actually something that feels more normal for the Chargers' offensive operation over the past few seasons. Whether it's efficiency or explosiveness, the Chargers have been outright poor this season. They rank 31st in overall success rate, only above the Eagles' offense having its own season from hell, and are dead last in passing success rate. The Chargers have only racked up an explosive gain on 8.3% of their plays this season, which ranks 31st. All this makes for a team that ranks dead last in EPA per play.

    It has been revealed that I could keep going. It's all bad, with nothing really to hang their hat on other than getting RB Omarion Hampton going a little bit recently, including a 105-yard performance in a Week 10 win over the Ravens.

    Recent findings suggest that mistakes hit this unit and position group with such regularity, it feels like a small miracle when the Chargers are even able to execute a play properly. Receivers are often redirected on routes or just end up with improper spacing in the passing game, sometimes with multiple players ending up in the same spot like they're about to play a game of red rover. Multiple blockers are too often going to the wrong assignment or to no assignment at all. For an offense that uses formational variety and tons of motion before the snap, Chargers players seem to be stretched too thin mentally, which has led to mistakes compounding any talent disadvantages they have (and boy do they have those).

    And even when those things do go right, Herbert is making weirdly too aggressive and incorrect decisions — he ranks last among qualifying quarterbacks in turnover rate — or a Chargers pass-catcher just drops the ball, sometimes even giving the football a volleyball set to a defender (the Chargers have 15 drops this year, by the way, which ranks 26th). Herbert's own spiraling this year has been a week-to-week car crash that is hard to look away from. His significant arm and longer throwing motion haven't mixed well with McDaniel's preferred quick-hitters off play action, and the lack of spacing has compounded the forays he has tried down the field. For an offense that seeks explosives, something McDaniel was able to seemingly generate by the dozen in Miami, it feels very tight, static, and just slow. And with nothing to alleviate the lack of spacing and separation in the passing game, and a run game that ranks bottom 10 in success rate and explosives, a pressing Herbert has spiraled the Chargers' offense into something like Charybdis.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday.
    • The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.
    • The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

    The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

    The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

    Recent findings suggest that just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

    MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE.

    Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

    Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

    Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

    AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

    Chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:.

    Recent findings suggest that he is among the new breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

    It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

    Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the fresh season.

    AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

    Possession: Chelsea 50%-50% AC MilanShots: 18-5Shots on target: 8-0Corners: 7-2.

    According to recent reports, the final whistle is blown in Jakarta and Chelsea have cruised to a 3-0 win over AC Milan. Goals from Caicedo and a double from Pedro either side of half-time have led Xabi Alonso’s side to the victory. They have one more game out in the Far East before returning home to the UK.

    Industry observers note that what a performance! 👏 pic.twitter.com/GcUZXwXbRj.

    Ramos is picked out after making a run into the Chelsea box and is denied by Sanchez. However, the offside flag has gone up anyway against Ramos. AC Milan have barely threatened the Chelsea goal in this second half.

    A late change for Chelsea as Sarr replaces Fofana.

    There will be five added minutes.

    Chelsea are seeking their fourth goal as Quenda strikes a shot powerfully from just outside the box but it goes narrowly wide. Xabi Alonso’s side have dominated this second half.

    Estevao has the chance to score moments after coming on after good work from the Brazilian down Chelsea’s right but is denied by a good save from Torriani.

    Industry observers note that chelsea make a triple changes as Estevao, Mudryk and Watson come on. Mudryk made his return after his doping ban against Juventus during the week.

    Industry observers note that chelsea hit the frame of the goal once more. Jackson gets the better of Vladimirov down Chelsea’s left and moves into the AC Milan penalty area. Jackson opens up his body as if he is going to curl his shot into the far corner but instead shoots towards the near corner, with his effort coming off the post.

    Ricci goes for an audacious strike with the outside of his right foot from outside the box but his effort misses the target.

    Palmer was deep in conversation with his boss Alonso during that water break.

    Sources indicate that chelsea made a substitution during that break as Anselmino comes on for Hato. Thus far, Chelsea have made three changes in this game and Alonso did confirm before the game that some players should be able to go the full 90 this far into pre-season.

    Time for the second half water break.

    Chelsea hit the post. Quenda receives the ball on the right side of the penalty area and quickly moves the ball onto his right foot. The 19-year-old then smashes a shot towards goal and the ball flies into the outside of the post. Quenda struck that with some venom.

    Palmer has a chance to get Chelsea’s fourth from the left side of the box but AC Milan keeper Torriani makes the save down to his left.

Pedro gets on the end of it and, despite the Milan keeper getting a touch on the shot, the ball ends up in the far corner.

    The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

    Sources indicate that yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

    Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

    Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

    In a recent development, “We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so vital to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”.

    It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

    AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

    The Kansas City Chiefs will likely be without Kenneth Walker III again for their Week 11 game against the Arizona Cardinals, head coach Andy Reid said Friday.

    Walker reported groin tightness last week, and the team decided to give him a rest and sit out the 35-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Reid said on Wednesday that the running back was "feeling better," but they did not "want to do something stupid.".

    On Friday, Reid remarked Walker, as well as offensive lineman Jaylon Moore and guard Trey Smith, are "improving" as they deal with injuries, but will "most likely" be ruled out.

    Rookie running back Emmett Johnson took advantage of the first-team opportunity and rushed for 101 yards on 22 carries, while adding six catches for 70 yards and two touchdowns in Week 10. He will be once again tasked with RB1 responsibilities as the 7-2 Chiefs look to win a third game in a row.

    It has been revealed that johnson, the team's fifth-round pick in the 2026 draft out of Nebraska, has 212 rushing yards and a touchdown, plus 20 receptions for 307 yards and three touchdowns this season. He has also served as the Chiefs' kick returner, picking up 318 return yards on 11 attempts.

    Through 10 weeks, Walker is fourth in rushing in the NFL with 872 yards and tied for fifth in the league among running backs with seven touchdowns.

    Recent findings suggest that the Chiefs have a short turnaround to prepare for Week 12. Following Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Kansas City will visit Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving Day. Could Walker be ready for that primetime matchup?

    According to recent reports, the Chiefs are understandably playing it safe with Walker, allowing the star to rest his groin injury after Johnson more than held his own in last week's blowout win. The rookie handled 22 carries and six receptions, leading to 32.1 half-PPR points on 20.6 expected points. Those are obviously elite RB1 numbers. Kansas City simply doesn't have another RB it trusts for the moment, and the offense is firing on all cylinders against mediocre opponents.

    The Cardinals are just that. They've allowed the fifth-most rush YPG (130) and were just schooled by Blake Corum (119 total yards) on Sunday. A huge 28-point team total as 15.5-point favorites (!!!!!!) awaits. I have Johnson as my overall RB2 for Week 11. — Hayden Winks.

The Raptors won't have RJ Barrett and Collin Murray-Boyles.

    In a recent development, using Yahoo projections, each player's last five games, the betting lines and the latest injury news, I ran 20,000 simulations of the slate against a simulated Yahoo field built from this week's pick rates. I'm paying up for the best player on the board and filling in around him with $2 and $3 players whose roles just got bigger. Here's my lineup:.

    This group finished in the top 1% of the simulated field 16.9% of the time — the best rate of the 20,000 lineups I tested — and beat every entry in the field more often than any other build (1.04%). Only about 0.03% of the field has these exact five.

    Industry observers note that jokić leads the slate at 54.00 projected fantasy points, more than three points clear of anyone else, on a line of 24.1 points, 10.7 rebounds, 8.9 assists, 1.7 steals and a block. I like the situational spot: Denver is a 3.5-point home favorite, and the 227.5 total is the highest on the slate. Yes, three-quarters of the field has him, but the matchup sets up well, too.

    Şengün took a shot to the face in Wednesday's win over Indiana and didn't return. Ime Udoka said he has swelling in his right eye and a scratched cornea in his left. If Şengün sits, Houston's answer for Jokić is Steven Adams, and a village. Houston won the first meeting 110-100 in Houston on Nov. 9; this one is in Denver. Fading Jokić is a real option in a top-heavy contest like this (see the contrarian build below), but my sims say he's worth going chalk.

    Jenkins is the best value on the board and I like him whether Cunningham plays or not. He's projected for 33.02 fantasy points at $3, ahead of several $4 players. He's been hot this week, too: 25 points, 5 rebounds and 5 assists in Tuesday's win over San Antonio, then 17 points and 9 assists as the starting point guard in Wednesday's win at New Orleans. Over his last five games, he's averaging about 36 fantasy points.

    Cunningham sat Wednesday with right knee soreness on the second night of a back-to-back, and he's questionable again Friday. The expectation is he plays. But if he sits, Jenkins runs the offense and his outlook gets even better. That built-in insurance is why he indicated up in the single best lineup in nearly 47% of my sims, more than any other player on the slate.

    It has been revealed that this is my leverage play. Walter is averaging 12.2 points, 2.5 3s and 1.3 steals, and he's projected for 27.15 fantasy points. What makes him interesting is everyone around him. Leonard and Barrett are out and Barnes is questionable after Toronto held him out of the back half of its back-to-back to manage his groin. Murray-Boyles is also in concussion protocol and won't play.

    Walter dropped 25 points with seven 3s against the Knicks on Tuesday, then followed it with 18 points, 7 rebounds, 6 assists and 3 steals against Washington. Toronto has lost six straight. Someone has to take shots, and he's shown he will. At 4% picked, he's the piece that separates this lineup from the field.

    Industry observers note that huerter was in the single best lineup in 45.3% of my simulations, second only to Jenkins. He's projected for 24.15 fantasy points at $2, and his role is growing with Detroit this banged-up. Robinson (left quad strain) will be re-evaluated in a week and Huerter started Wednesday, finishing with 11 points and 7 assists. He's hit double figures in five of his last six games, while averaging 33.1 minutes a night over that span. He's a cheap source of points, 3s, assists and the occasional block, and he doesn't need Cunningham to sit to pay off.

    It has been revealed that johnson is the second-most popular pick in my lineup. He's projected for 23.13 fantasy points at $2, starting next to Jokić in the slate's highest-scoring game. He's averaging 11.4 points, 3.7 rebounds, 1.7 3s and 1.1 steals, a steady floor for the price. His recent body of work is meh (about 21 fantasy points a game over his last five), but he still landed in the optimal lineup about a third of the time. You don't get leverage from him, but you get it from Walter and Jenkins, and that's enough. I'm banking on a bounce-back from the 15.9 fantasy points he scored in 31 minutes versus Houston on Nov. 9.

    Using Yahoo's projections, the highest-scoring possible lineup is Jokić, Cunningham, Huerter, Johnson and Alijah Martin at 161.63 fantasy points. Mine comes in just 0.18 points behind it.

    Sources indicate that on paper, it's the max. In the sims, it finished in the top 1% only 6.6% of the time, less than half the rate of my lineup. Two things hurt it. First, Cunningham's knee: a questionable tag means there's a real chance he sits. Second, Martin is a $1 punt projected under 10 points, so you're leaning on two players to carry the build. Swapping Cunningham and Martin for Jenkins and Walter gives up 0.18 projected points and removes most of that risk.

    If you want to get away from the 76% of the field on Jokić, this was the best lineup without him:.

    It reached the top 1% of the field 12.6% of the time and beat the entire field in 1.01% of sims, nearly matching my main lineup's win rate, and essentially nobody in the simulated field has these five.

    Breaking: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

    📅 08 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2627 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.
    • Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.
    • The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

    Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

    The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

    But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

    “He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

    “We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”.

    Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

    Recent findings suggest that michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl.

    United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

    Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

    United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

    United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

    Industry observers note that “It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”.

    Industry observers note that “It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a big season ahead.”.

    “It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”.

    “We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have big season and hope to win a trophy.”.

    It has been revealed that all over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

    Nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

    Fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

    According to recent reports, two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right. He chips the ball to the back post where one of the Fletchers (sorry, I am not sure which) heads for goal. His attempt is blocked and the ball, ultimately, falls at the feet of Lacey whose shot is blazed high over the bar.

    According to recent reports, there have been plenty of good things for Carrick to take from this match. The passing, while not of the standard of a cut-and-thrust Premier League match, has been good for the time of year, and there have been enough flashes of brilliance/class/invention etc to suggest that pre-season is moving in the right direction.

    Lovely bit of play by United. A great pass with the outside of the boot from the inside-left channel by Tielemans finds Fernandes who plays a sidefooted shot that goes just wide.

    Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

    Industry observers note that both sides losing possession a fair bit at the moment. Strong pre-season vibes right now.

    Maguire has had a good game. He’s played a number of long passes from the back and looked assured. This time he’s up in the PSG half and decides to have a pop - his shot testing Safanov, who saves well.

    Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

    Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

    Recent findings suggest that chance for United to go ahead and it comes from two things. (i) A long, hopeful ball from Fernandes that looks for Zirkzee (ii) Safanov rushing off his line and into no-man’s land. The ball comes loose and Jack Fletcher, instead of having a go at goal, with the keeper on the ground and out of the game, passes to Lacey whose shot is wide.

    Sources indicate that tyler Fletcher loses the ball near the United half and it, ultimately, results in a PSG corner. From the set piece United defend well and snuff out all hint of danger.

    According to recent reports, PSG seeing more of the ball at the moment. They work the ball to the right and Amass brings down Mbaye.

    From the resulting free-kick, in the final third, the French side whip in the ball but Mee is up ot the challenge and come to collect well.

    Santos, Mbeumo, Shaw, Amad, Lacey are off.

    Fernandes, Jack Feltcher, Zirkzee and Amass are on.

    And it’s a debut for Tielemans.

    A raft of changes for PSG sees Marquinhos and João Neves, among others, come on. More like it, in terms of first-team ‘names’, on the pitch for the European Cup champions.

    United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

    The paces quickens and the game is much better for it. Mbuemo drives toward the PSG box, he cuts inside from the right before unleashing a shot that is bound for the back of the net before a fine one-handed save by Safanov. Credit, too, for Maguire whose long ball from the back found Mbuemo brilliantly. Promising...

    Lacey tries to play in Dorgu on the left but he’s asking too much of his team-mate. Wonder when the expected raft of changes will take place?

    Slow start to the second half. This is very much pre-season-friendly pace.

    Sources indicate that having seen Mount limp off in the first half, there’s more worry at the start of the second and Heaton is force off with what looks like a hamstrung injury. He dashed off his line to clear a ball and in doing so has tweaked something. Mee replaces him.

    Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

    A world record that still stands...(this was back in 1995).

    It has been revealed that and that is it for the first 45 minutes. PSG took the early lead, but from that moment on United have been the better side and deservedly are level through Mbueno’s goal.

    There will be one minute of added time at the end of what has been a good first half for Man Utd.

    In a recent development, amad has a go from outside the box forcing the save from Safanov. He’s such a live wire and one of the best in his position in the top flight. Him or Antony? No contest, strange it took United a while to work that one out.

    Yet more good work from the underrated Amad. He again closes down well on the right before winning back possession and cutting the ball back for Lacey. To think he was starring for Sunderland in the Championship while Antony was starting for United...

    Sources indicate that united have been the better side since conceding earlier and, as if to illustrate my point, as I typed that an Mbuemo free-kick is well saved by Safanov. That was heading for the top-right bin.

    Recent findings suggest that great work on the left by Dorgu and Shaw ends with the latter chipping the ball to the back post where Amad is lurking with intent. The Ivorian looks to head the ball home, but before he can get anything on it it looks as though he’s pushed in the back. United players are sure it’s a penalty but, more importantly, the referee doesn’t.

    Amad does brilliantly, winning the ball off Koukaba in the final third, from there he scampers toward the box before playing in Mbuemo who takes one touch before firing in a shot into the bottom right corner of the net.

    Sources indicate that free-kick for PSG on the right, near the final third. The ball comes in and it’s straight into the arms of Heaton in the United goal.

    Kvaratskhelia, not seen much of him so far, runs into the box, but Amad does well to usher him back out.

    The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

    United continue to see more of the ball, Dorgu’s seeing more of it than most. But, no chances really fashioned, still, plenty of time to go.

    Recent findings suggest that worry for United having to sub off Mount. It looks as though he took a knock to a foot and Carrick and co will hope it’s not a long-term injury. Mount, who’s had a good pre-season, has been replaced by Fletcher, son of Darren.

    Foul on Mazraoui results in two things. The Mount has to come off, and, United have a free-kick on the edge of the PSG area.

    From the set-piece Mbuemo has a go and it’s a regulation save from Safonov in the PSG goal.

    Heaven loses possession in the middle of the park and from there it’s like the parting of the Red Sea as PSG have a three-on-one. Mbaye gets the shot in on goal but Andrey Santos covers back brilliantly and does enough to get something on the ball. He’s started both this match and pre-season well.

    United are looking half decent on the ball. They’re passing it well and not afraid to switch things around.

    Sources indicate that A lovely long ball from Maguire finds Dorgo whose lovely first touch takes him into the box before a cut back is intercepted by a PSG man. Promising signs though for Carrick’s men.

    United seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

    Needless to say this is being played at a slowish pace...no blood-and-guts challenges being put in.

    It has been revealed that good work down the right sees Amad plays in Shay Lacey who crosses into the box. The ball find shte head of Mbuemo and the ball sails over the bar. Better from United.

    United started slowly against Atletico and they’ve done the same here.

    Bright start to say the least from the French side. They work the ball left and it’s an easy cross from Dro Fernandez for Mbaye to tap home for the very early lead.

    Industry observers note that they’re under way in Sweden. United are in their new vibrant red kit and PSG in their blue, red and white kit. Major fan of the French side’s kit, it harks back to the kit they had in the 1990s when the likes of George Weah and David Ginola were entertaining in the capital of France.

    A reminder of how they line up.

    Industry observers note that man Utd: Heaton, Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw, Mount, Santos, Dorgu, Lacey, Amad, Mbeumo; Subs: Heath, Mee, Amass, Armer, Dalot, Yoro, Fernandes, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Tielemans, Zirkzee.

    Paris St-Germain: Safonov, Pacho, Zabarnyi, Koukaba, Boly, Beraldo, Dro, Mayulu, Kvaratskhelia, Ayari, Mbaye; Subs: Marquinhos, Mendes, Lucea, Vitinha, Neves, El Nay, Idder, Drame, Bourdin, Ndjantou, Meite, Longoni, Chevalier.

    And here’s a famous match that took place there, giving a certain Sir Alex Ferguson his first European trophy.

    “Get a bit sharper, get better on the ball, go up a notch.”.

    Sources indicate that “It’s not about today it’s about preparing. Some players have played 90 minutes, some have played three games, some have just come back. So it’s about keeping working on things we’ve been working on.”.

    According to recent reports, “They’re similar to us, but have fewer senior players available . They’ve had a great time and great squad so whoever on the pitch it will be a test.”.

    A hugely talented player for a number of clubs, including United, who ever really lived up to his early promise.

    Here’s a goal to dine out on...

    Good to have you back, lads 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/3EgkXLqcQm.

    Industry observers note that 📃 Le onze de départ pour cette rencontre de préparation face à Manchester United. #PSGMUN pic.twitter.com/LodcDM1Yrm.

    I expect they’ll make an appearence at some point.

    Ready to face PSG in our latest pre-season test ✊.

    Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

    Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how latest signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

    Industry observers note that one of those latest signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

    Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

    It has been revealed that cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

    This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

    It has been revealed that “I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

    “The spirit and the camaraderie is so vital for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s organization. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”.

    Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

    • The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.

    The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

    Sources indicate that that goal also was supposed to set up penalties. But after minutes of waiting around – and Kevin Campello, Chelsea’s head of first-team operations, saying “it’s written in the contract” – the players walked off the pitch.

    That confusion ended a feisty affair in which tensions threatened to boil over and that, at certain points, paid little attention to the “friendly” aspect of the clash with seven yellow cards shown. At one point the visitors’ latest set-piece coach Austin MacPhee exchanged angry words with some of Johor’s coaching staff. The CFC TV commentary team suggested that the spot-kicks were abandoned because of the match’s heated atmosphere.

    Austin MacPhee was ready to throw hands😂 pic.twitter.com/CFDgTOwmxE.

    Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters given much-needed game time.

    And considering Johor are one game away from setting a new world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight – a run that would surpass the current mark set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s – it was also no shock to see the Malaysian team offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

    Sources indicate that after a good start Chelsea were second best in a first half in which Johor should have been at least two goals to the good. The Malaysian champions controlled the first 45 minutes and were 1-0 up after 14 minutes – a low cross from the left side-footed home by Arif Aiman.

    The hosts gave the young, inexperienced Chelsea backline a torrid time, especially on the flanks and Óscar Arribas was guilty of not capitalising on a great chance to double Johor’s lead, his shot after cutting in from the right going wide.

    Recent findings suggest that while they looked vulnerable at the back, Chelsea also struggled to keep possession in attack. But they got an equaliser they scarcely deserved after Liam Delap was manhandled to the ground in the box by Kevin Medina. The striker, who may well leave Stamford Bridge before the transfer window slams shut, fired home the spot-kick allowing the visitors to go into the break on level terms.

    For the most part, the second half followed a similar pattern to the first – Jofor having the better chances, while tensions on the pitch continued to run high.

    It was, however, Chelsea who took the lead after the break, Delap once again scoring from the spot, this time after Jamie Gittens was brought down in the area.

    Johor, though, kept on creating, thanks in part to a fairly porous visitors’ backline, and levelled through a deflected Arribas free kick, before going 3-2 up thanks thanks to a well-taken Bérgson strike.

    According to recent reports, had it stayed that way Chelsea could have had few complaints. But as the clock approached 90 minutes, the visitors had one last attack. Mykhailo Mudryk, just on as a substitute, delivered a cross from the left that Antonio Glauder could only steer into his own net. That was supposed to set up the penalty shoot-out that did not take place and the chance for one of the sides to claim a hollow victory.

    Considering a raft of changes and that fact this was far from the first XI, it is hard to know what to make of this. But among the positive things Alonso could take from the game was the impressive form of Nicolas Jackson and good centre-forward play of Delap. The negative was, however, a poor defensive display.

    Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday for their last pre-season friendly, against Real Sociedad, before the Premier League season starts away at local rivals Fulham on August 24.

    A mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters you may not have heard of.

    Recent findings suggest that johor Darul Ta’Zim – more commonly known as JDT – are the Man Utd of Malaysia (at least that’s according to a Malaysian friend of mine). In 2013, they were going nowhere and were the dictionary definition of a stagnant club, low on confidence and trophies. That was until the Crown Prince bought the club and, over the next 13 years, transformed it into the powerhouse it is today.

    As if to underline JDT’s dominance over Malaysian football they are one game away from the world record unbeaten run in a top flight. The new season of the Malaysian Super League gets under way later this month and should they avoid defeat in their opening match they will extend their unbeaten run - which began in April 2021 - to 109 games and surpass the world record set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s.

    Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

    A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

    The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

    Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

    In a recent development, just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

    Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

    “The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

    “We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our initiative and we’ve stuck to that.

    “We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”.

    Patriots QB Drake Maye reportedly has fractured right fibula, could return later this season

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Following testing, Upcoming England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye reportedly suffered a fractured right fibula in Week 10, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Mike Reiss.
    • Maye will not require surgery and there is a small chance he could be back for the Patriots late in the regular season if they are contending for an AFC playoff spot.
    • In a recent development, maye sustained the injury during the team's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Following testing, Upcoming England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye reportedly suffered a fractured right fibula in Week 10, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Mike Reiss.

    Maye will not require surgery and there is a small chance he could be back for the Patriots late in the regular season if they are contending for an AFC playoff spot.

    In a recent development, maye sustained the injury during the team's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday. It happened on the team's first drive, which ended after Maye was sacked by Lions star Aidan Hutchinson.

    Maye's injury actually wasn't the focus initially. Following the sack, Hutchinson sustained a torn ACL while celebrating the play. He'll miss the rest of the season due to the injury.

    In a recent development, the true extent of Maye's injury came to light on the Patriots' next offensive drive. Backup Tommy DeVito entered the game in place of Maye, who was spotted on the broadcast walking back to the team's locker room. Maye was unable to return to the game, and the team was tight-lipped about the nature of the injury.

    Later Sunday, reports started to emerge suggesting Maye could miss "a while." Those reports received more clarity Monday, when it was revealed Maye remained in Germany to receive further evaluation. By Monday morning, it was reported the Patriots feared Maye was dealing with a "significant lower leg injury," possibly a fracture.

    According to recent reports, the injury could end Maye's third NFL season prematurely. While the 24-year-old got off to a tough start, turning the ball over seven times in the team's first three games, he proved last year's excellence was not a fluke. In the six games leading up to Week 10, Maye had 17 passing touchdowns against five interceptions. He was on pace for yet another strong year before the injury.

    While Maye's long-term outlook remains strong, the Patriots' short-term outlook appears disastrous. Following the team's loss in Week 10, the Patriots sit at 5-5 through 10 games. The playoffs are still very much in the picture, but only if the team can rally around its new quarterback. That didn't happen in Week 10, as the team looked listless with DeVito under center.

    But DeVito will have the bye week to get fully up to speed. When the Patriots return to action, they'll take on the 1-8 Los Angeles Chargers, giving DeVito an opportunity for a substantial game in his first start.

    After that, though, things get much harder for the Patriots. During the last six weeks of the regular season, New England will take on the Buffalo Bills, Minnesota Vikings, Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos. The team very likely needs to win at least two, possibly three of those games to secure a spot in the postseason.

    Getting that done without Maye will be extremely difficult.

    Padres' Mason Miller, Blue Jays' Louis Varland named MLB Relievers of the Year in first-ever BBWAA award

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (581 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller and Toronto Blue Jays closer Louis Varland have been named the winners of the first-ever Baseball Writers Association of America Reliever of the Year award.
    • The BBWAA's Reliever of the Year award is separate from the Mariano Rivera Award and Trevor Hoffman Award, which honor the best relievers in the American League and National League, respectively.
    • Like the other BBWAA awards, the new Reliever of the Year award is voted on by BBWAA members (two per MLB city in each league).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller and Toronto Blue Jays closer Louis Varland have been named the winners of the first-ever Baseball Writers Association of America Reliever of the Year award. The BBWAA introduced the award this year and, moving forward, will hand it out annually along with Rookies and Managers of the Year, Cy Young, and MVPs.

    The BBWAA's Reliever of the Year award is separate from the Mariano Rivera Award and Trevor Hoffman Award, which honor the best relievers in the American League and National League, respectively. The Rivera and Hoffman Awards replaced the Delivery Man of the Year Award in 2015 and are voted on by a panel of former relievers, including Rivera and Hoffman.

    Like the other BBWAA awards, the new Reliever of the Year award is voted on by BBWAA members (two per MLB city in each league). Votes were submitted before the beginning of the playoffs, meaning that only regular-season contributions are taken into account.

    The best closer in baseball is the first-ever BBWAA National League Reliever of the Year. Miller was overwhelming from start to finish this past season, pitching to a 1.67 ERA with 129 strikeouts in only 70 innings. He led all pitchers with 3.9 WAR, well ahead of second-place Louie Varland (3.1 WAR), and he led the NL in saves (38) and games finished (57).

    Miller's strikeout rate lapped the field. Here are the highest strikeout rates (strikeouts per batter faced) among qualified relievers:.

    Sources indicate that miller just completed his first full season with the Padres. He was acquired from the Athletics at the 2025 trade deadline at a very high cost: San Diego sent shortstop Leo De Vries, one of the best prospects in baseball, to the A's in the six-player deal. Miller has been worth the price, though. He owns a 1.45 ERA in parts of two seasons with the Padres.

    This is the first major award of Miller's career, who finished fourth in the 2024 AL Rookie of the Year voting and has two All-Star Game selections (2024 and 2026), but otherwise had never received Cy Young or MVP votes prior to this season. He beat out the Brewers' Trevor Megill and Phillies' Jhoan Duran for the award.

    According to recent reports, after jumping into the national spotlight with his high usage during the 2025 postseason, Varland is the first winner of the BBWAA American League Reliever of the Year award. His 1.27 ERA led qualified relievers and his 3.1 WAR was tops in the AL. Varland struck out 87 batters in 78 innings and was fifth with 35 saves. He won with his sheer dominance, not his saves total.

    In a recent development, varland was a workhorse for the Blue Jays this year, much like he was last October. He finished second in saves of at least four outs during the regular season:.

    Sources indicate that the Blue Jays acquired Varland from the Minnesota Twins, his hometown team, at the 2025 trade deadline. He struggled initially after the deal, posting a 4.94 ERA with Toronto after the deadline, but Varland found his footing in the postseason and then found another gear in 2026. He was one of the game's best relievers and a true workhorse.

    Sources indicate that varland was an All-Star for the first time this season. This was also his first year receiving any award votes. He beat out the Guardians' Cade Smith and Rays' Bryan Baker for the award.
